title: Uniqueness and basepoint freeness of a degree-two pencil
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective] of genus $g\geq2$ [def-sc-genus]. For an effective divisor $D$ on $C$ [def-sc-divisor], let $|D|$ be the set of effective divisors linearly equivalent to $D$, where linear equivalence means that the difference is a principal divisor. The scheme of members of $|D|$ is the projective space of one-dimensional subspaces of $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))$ (nonzero sections modulo scalars). If $\deg D=2$ and $|D|$ has two distinct members, then $\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))=2$, and $|D|$ is basepoint free: no point belongs to every member. There is at most one such complete degree-two linear system on $C$. In that system, for every $Q\in C(k)$ there is exactly one member containing $Q$. Equivalently, any nonconstant degree-two map $C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ has these members as its fibre divisors, and any two such maps differ by an automorphism of $\mathbf P^1_k$.

source.place: Chapter III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), printed p.120, first paragraph recalling the unique degree-two dimension-one linear system (citing Hartshorne IV §5), and the two-divisor argument in the following paragraphs. Applies in arbitrary characteristic.

proof.text: The projective curve $C$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $C$ is Noetherian and integral. Put $L=\mathcal O_C(D)$. The divisor-class isomorphism [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] makes this an invertible sheaf and identifies linear equivalence with equality of its Picard class. Its degree in [def-sc-pic0] is $2$. This agrees with the Euler-characteristic degree used by [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound]: [lem-sc-riemann-roch] gives $\chi(N)-\chi(\mathcal O_C)=\deg N$ for every invertible $N$. We use this agreement for all line bundles below. Their spaces of sections are finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (proper curve over the Noetherian field, invertible sheaf coherent).

The section/divisor dictionary here is explicit: a nonzero $f\in H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))\subset k(C)$ gives the effective divisor $D+\operatorname{div}(f)$, by the valuation inequalities of [def-sc-divisor]. Every effective divisor equivalent to $D$ has this form. Two such sections give the same divisor exactly when their ratio has divisor zero; it and its inverse are then global functions by those same inequalities. They are nonzero scalars by [lem-sc-global-functions]. Thus the two distinct members give two independent sections of $L$. This also gives the nonzero-sections-modulo-scalars parametrization used to define the scheme of members in the statement.

Apply [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound] with $U=H^0(C,L)$ and $q=\dim U\ge2$. Its generated line has degree $0\le a\le2$, and $q\le\max\{a+1-g,a/2+1\}\le2$. Hence $q=2$. Every closed point is $k$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. If a closed point $Q$ belonged to every member, the valuation formula would give $U\subset H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D-Q))$. Apply the same bound to this two-dimensional subspace of a degree-one line bundle: $a\le1$ would give $2\le\max\{a+1-g,a/2+1\}\le3/2$, impossible. Thus there is no base point. In local generators of $L$ [lem-sc-divisor-module-local], this says some section is a unit at each closed point; the nonzero sections also generate at the generic point. Therefore evaluation generates $L$ everywhere.

source.place: III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120, expanded using the RR/Clifford bound

proof.text: Fix $Q\in C(k)$. Evaluation $H^0(C,L)\to L\otimes k(Q)$ is a nonzero linear map from a two-dimensional space to a one-dimensional space, by basepoint freeness. Its kernel is exactly one line. Its nonzero sections, modulo scalars, give exactly the members containing $Q$ by the local valuation formula of [def-sc-divisor]. Thus there is exactly one such member, including when that member is $2Q$.

source.place: III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120, fibres as members

proof.text: Suppose $|E|$ is another moving complete system of degree two and set $M=\mathcal O_C(E)$. The preceding arguments give bases $s_0,s_1$ of $H^0(C,L)$ and $t_0,t_1$ of $H^0(C,M)$, both generating their line bundles. Degrees add under tensor product by [def-sc-pic0], so $\deg(L\otimes M)=4$. If the four products $s_it_j$ were independent, their span $U$ would have dimension four. Applied to $U\subset H^0(C,L\otimes M)$, [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound] gives $a\le4$ and $4\le\max\{a+1-g,a/2+1\}\le3$, a contradiction. Thus there is a nonzero relation $s_0a+s_1b=0$ with $a,b\in H^0(C,M)$, obtained by grouping the coefficients of the four products by $s_i$. Since $t_0,t_1$ are a basis and the coefficient vector is nonzero, $(a,b)\ne(0,0)$.

source.place: III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120, uniqueness recalled there; agent pencil-trick expansion

proof.text: On the open where $s_1$ generates $L$, put $z=a/s_1\in\Gamma(M\otimes L^{-1})$; on the open where $s_0$ generates, put $z=-b/s_0$. The relation makes these equal on the overlap, so they glue. These two opens cover $C$, and the same relation gives $a=s_1z$ and $b=-s_0z$ on both opens. Consequently $z\ne0$, since $(a,b)\ne(0,0)$. By [def-sc-pic0], $\deg(M\otimes L^{-1})=0$. By [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity], $z$ cannot vanish anywhere: a zero would force strictly positive degree. A nowhere vanishing section trivializes an invertible sheaf (locally its coefficient is a unit), so $M\simeq L$. The divisor-class isomorphism [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] now gives $E\sim D$, hence $|E|=|D|$.

source.place: Tag 0B40, lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial (2); explicit local pencil-trick calculation supplied by agent

proof.text: A basis $s_0,s_1$ of $H^0(C,L)$ defines $f=[s_0:s_1]:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ with $f^*\mathcal O(1)\simeq L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] and its construction over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections]. It is nonconstant: if the ratio were constant, the two sections would be dependent. The projective line is a smooth proper connected curve by [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero]. The function-field correspondence [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] gives dominance and a finite function-field extension. A coordinate section of $\mathcal O(1)$ has a single simple zero on the standard affine charts, so its divisor degree is one; [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section], [def-sc-pic0] and [lem-sc-riemann-roch], now applied to the projective line, give the same Euler-characteristic degree one. Hence [lem-sfb-proper-curve-bundle-pullback-degree] gives $[k(C):k(\mathbf P^1)]=\deg L=2$. Locally the fibre above $[u:v]$ is the zero divisor of $v s_0-u s_1$; these sections run through every nonzero section modulo scalar, exactly giving $|D|$ with multiplicities.

The map $f$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the separated target $\mathbf P^1$. Its fibre over a closed target point is supported on the zeros of the corresponding nonzero section, hence on a finite divisor. Apply [thm-sc-proper-finite-fibre-finite-neighbourhood] at every closed target point (the target is Noetherian by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]). These neighbourhoods cover all closed points and also the generic point, which belongs to every nonempty open. Those are all points of this curve by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Thus they cover the target and $f$ is finite. This verifies the finite-map formulation recalled by Milne without any separability hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0CCL, lemma-finite, proof by proper finite-fibre neighbourhoods

proof.text: Conversely let $h:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be nonconstant of degree two. Its induced function-field extension is finite by [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms]. Set $N=h^*\mathcal O(1)$. The pullback degree formula [lem-sfb-proper-curve-bundle-pullback-degree] gives $\deg N=2$. The coordinate sections pull back to two independent generating sections: generation follows from the projective-space dictionary [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points], and a linear relation would force $h$ to be constant. For a nonzero pulled-back section $s$, its rational-section divisor [def-sc-rational-section-divisor] is effective, and [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section] identifies $N$ with $\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}s)$. Thus its zero divisor has degree two and the different sections give linearly equivalent divisors; the section bound and uniqueness already proved show that they form the unique complete system. Finally two such maps are defined by two bases of its same two-dimensional section space, after identifying their line bundles. The change of basis is an invertible $2\times2$ matrix. Its linear action on homogeneous coordinates defines an automorphism of $\mathbf P^1$, with inverse given by the inverse matrix, and sends the first map to the second.
